workflow.purpose:
Create or update a system document in `{docs_path}/wiki/subsystems/[subsystem-name]/systems/`.
A system doc describes a coherent domain system — WHAT exists, HOW it works, WHERE things live. It is the primary document an AI agent reads before implementing a related story.
This workflow is executed directly — NO sub-agents are spawned. The executing agent does everything: finding relevant code, reading it, analyzing components/flows, and writing the document.
workflow.docs-root:
Every `{docs_path}` below is a placeholder, not a literal path. Its value is the `docs_path` field from this skill's init output (read from `.ace/settings.json`, preprocessed into the prompt above). Substitute the real value before you read, write, glob or `mkdir` any documentation path.
It is `.docs` in a typical single-project repo, but monorepos commonly nest it — `ProcerERP/.docs`, for example. Typing a literal `.docs` in a project that nests its docs creates a second, orphaned documentation tree at the repo root: the files appear to be written successfully, but every other ACE command resolves the configured root and will never find them.
When you spawn a subagent, state the resolved root explicitly in its prompt (e.g. `Docs root: ProcerERP/.docs`) and substitute it into every path you hand it. A subagent starts with a fresh context — it cannot see the init output you are holding, so an unsubstituted `{docs_path}` reaches it as literal text.
If `docs_path` is missing from the init output, stop and tell the user to run `/ace:help`, which detects and pins the location — do not guess.
workflow.mandatory-context: All supporting resource files are auto-loaded in the skill prompt above. Do NOT re-read them. Also read any document or text passed as parameter ($ARGUMENTS) in the invoking command.

process.step:
Display stage banner:
``` ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ ACE > Map System Doc ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ```
Parse $ARGUMENTS for: `text`, `subsystem`, `story-context`, `commits`.
**If `text` is missing:** Ask the user: - header: "System Doc" - question: "Describe the system to document — what domain concern does it address?\nE.g., 'Drawing system - manages all drawing tools on the chart'"
**If `subsystem` is missing:** Ask the user: - header: "System Doc" - question: "Which subsystem does this system belong to?"
Resolve the subsystem. Check if `{docs_path}/wiki/subsystems/[subsystem-name]/` exists.
**If not found:** ``` ! No wiki found for subsystem "[subsystem]". Run /ace:map-subsystem first to create the subsystem wiki. ``` Exit.
Ensure systems directory exists: ```bash mkdir -p {docs_path}/wiki/subsystems/[subsystem_name]/systems ```
Display: ``` i System: [text description] Subsystem: [subsystem-name] Story context: [path/issue, or "none"] Commits: [value, or "search codebase directly"] ```
Continue to step 2.

Scan for existing system docs:
``` Glob(pattern='*.md', path='{docs_path}/wiki/subsystems/[subsystem_name]/systems') ```
**If existing system docs found:** Read their titles and overview sections. Check if any covers the same or overlapping domain concern.
**If overlap detected:** Use AskUserQuestion: - header: "System Doc" - question: "An existing system doc may cover a similar concern:\n\n- `[existing-file]`: [title]\n\nShould I update the existing doc or create a new one?" - options: - "Update existing" — set MODE = update, set TARGET_FILE = existing path - "Create new" — set MODE = create
**If no overlap or no existing docs:** Set MODE = create.
**If MODE = create:** Derive file name from the system description in kebab-case. Set TARGET_FILE = `{docs_path}/wiki/subsystems/[subsystem_name]/systems/[system-name].md`
Continue to step 3.

Read all markdown files in the story artifacts folder. Extract a brief summary of intent: what was built and why.
```bash gh issue view [issue-number] --json title,body,labels,comments ``` Extract a brief summary of intent from the issue.
Skip — rely on code analysis only.
```bash git diff --name-only HEAD~[N]..HEAD ``` Filter to files within the subsystem. Read each file.
```bash git diff --name-only [first-sha]^..[last-sha] ``` Filter to files within the subsystem. Read each file.
Use the `text` description to identify the system's files:
1. Read the subsystem's structure.md and architecture.md for orientation 2. Grep for keywords from the text description (class names, domain terms) 3. Follow imports/references to find all files belonging to this system 4. Read each discovered file
**Be thorough.** A system doc covers an entire domain concern. Follow class hierarchies, interface implementations, DI registrations, and cross-references until you have the complete picture.
For every source file found, understand:
- Class hierarchies and interface implementations - Entry points (API endpoints, event handlers, user actions) - Data flow through all layers (trace E2E for sequence diagrams) - State management (Redux, local state, database) - Constants, enums, and configuration - Integration points (imports from other systems, events) - Error handling and propagation - DI registrations, factory/registry entries
Build a mental model of the complete system.
Continue to step 4.

Read ALL existing wiki docs under `{docs_path}/wiki/subsystems/[subsystem_name]/` for cross-referencing in the Related Systems section.
Follow the system template structure exactly.
- Overview: ONE paragraph — what the system DOES, why it exists - File Tree: ALL files belonging to this system with purpose annotations (ASCII only)
Build a mermaid graph diagram showing what is INSIDE vs OUTSIDE this system.
Build a mermaid classDiagram for inheritance chains and interface implementations. Include key contracts inline (interfaces/types only). Omit if hierarchy is trivial (1 class, no inheritance).
List every "front door" into this system with `file:ClassName.method` references.
**MANDATORY — never skip.** Write at least one mermaid sequenceDiagram showing complete E2E data flow. One diagram per key behavior (1-5 behaviors typically). Show COMPLETE flow from entry point through all layers to data store and back.
Write all remaining applicable sections from the template: - Components (location, purpose, key interface) - Key Behaviors (trigger, logic, effect) - State Management (where, what shape, transitions) - Error Propagation (throw/catch chain) - Constants and Enums (exact file paths — agents must never hardcode) - Related Systems (cross-reference with markdown links) - Integration Points - Configuration and Options - Database (only if applicable) - Gotchas
Omit sections that genuinely don't apply. NEVER omit Data Flow.
**If MODE = create:** Write the complete document to TARGET_FILE. **If MODE = update:** Read the existing doc, ADD/expand sections, preserve unchanged content, match existing style, write to TARGET_FILE.
Continue to step 5.

Re-read TARGET_FILE and verify:
50+ lines of substantial content Overview present (ONE paragraph) File Tree present with purpose annotations (ASCII only) System Boundary mermaid diagram present At least one mermaid sequenceDiagram in Data Flow section (MANDATORY) Entry Points listed with file:Symbol references Components listed with location, purpose, key interface Constants and Enums locations documented Code references use `file:Symbol` format, not line numbers No pseudocode, no fabricated code, no filler phrases No ASCII arrows for architecture/flows (all mermaid) Related Systems cross-referenced with markdown links
Fix any failures by editing the document directly.
``` Grep( pattern="(sk-[a-zA-Z0-9]{20,}|sk_live_|sk_test_|ghp_[a-zA-Z0-9]{36}|AKIA[A-Z0-9]{16}|-----BEGIN.*PRIVATE KEY)", path="[TARGET_FILE]", output_mode="content" ) ```
SECRETS_FOUND — alert user, do NOT commit. CLEAN.
```bash git add [TARGET_FILE] git commit -m "docs([subsystem_name]): add system doc — [system-name]" ```
Display:
``` ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ ACE > Map System Doc > Complete ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
+ [TARGET_FILE] ([line count] lines)
System: [text description] Sections: [list of sections written] Sequence diagrams: [count]
Next > /clear first for a fresh context window, then:
/ace:map-sys-doc — create another system document /ace:map-pattern — document a pattern used by this system /ace:map-guide — create a how-to guide for this system Review file at [TARGET_FILE] ```
End workflow.

success_criteria.criterion: System description parsed and subsystem validated
Relevant source files discovered (from commits or codebase search)
All source files read and analyzed for components, flows, state, errors
Existing docs checked to avoid duplication (create vs update decision)
System doc follows template structure from system.xml
At least one mermaid sequenceDiagram present (E2E flow mandatory)
File tree uses ASCII only, no Unicode box-drawing
All diagrams use mermaid, no ASCII arrows for architecture/flows
Code references use file:Symbol format, no line numbers
Related systems cross-referenced with markdown links
No filler, no pseudocode, no fabricated code
